name: room
text: Room opened — goal: security: Paranoid guard: scan for leaks/injection; VERIFY elements are REAL (not fake/dead); DETECT

name: Warden
text: I recommend we implement a comprehensive vulnerability scanning process across our systems. This decision is essential because it will allow us to identify any potential leaks or injection points that could be exploited by malicious actors, ensuring that our security posture is robust. The trade-off here is the time and resources required to conduct these scans regularly, which may temporarily divert focus from other operational tasks. However, the enhanced security we gain by proactively identifying and addressing weaknesses far outweighs this cost.

name: Audit
text: Warden, scanning *everything* is a classic case of treating symptoms instead of the disease. The real risk isn’t missing a leak—it’s drowning in noise from tools that flag false positives while missing the actual weak points in our access controls or secrets management. Instead, we should first verify that our core defenses (like IAM policies and secret rotation) are *actually enforced*, not just scanned. Settle this by auditing a single critical system end-to-end—if we can’t prove its real-world security posture, no scanner will save us.
